title: add-benchmark-lab-adaptive-batching-reporting-pipeline-v98
author: Ayesha Patel
description: Motivation: extend the Benchmark Lab to collect adaptive-batching telemetry and produce a consolidated reporting pipeline that correlates batching decisions with end-to-end latency and cost. This PR adds a representative adaptive-batching workload runner, profiling baselines for adaptive scenarios, and a reporting DAG that ingests profiler outputs and exposes per-run metrics (batch size distribution, queue latency, scheduling latency, token cost delta). Changes include a small migration to the benchmark-lab schema (optional backward-compatible fields) and a new CI job that runs the adaptive runner on the perf canary image. Checklist: - add adaptive batching runner and config - add profiling baselines and example workloads - add reporting DAG and SQL transforms - update docs and examples - add CI integration for nightly perf runs Notes: kept the schema change backwards compatible (added batch_mode field with default "static"). The description below contains a short summary of commits, changed files, review conversation, and CI results.

release_notes:
- Added adaptive batching runner and reporting pipeline for Benchmark Lab.
- New metrics: batch_size_distribution, p95_queue_latency, scheduling_latency, token_cost_delta.
- Backwards-compatible schema change: added 'batch_mode' with default 'static' (no action required).
- Nightly CI job added to exercise adaptive scenarios.
notes: This PR is primarily for internal benchmarking. The reporting DAG outputs are consumed by benchmark-lab dashboards (Grafana) and the perf analytics pipeline. The changes were stress-tested on the perf canary image across small GPU instances and the baseline results are checked into profiling/baselines. Rolling back is low risk: the default is static batching and the new DAG is additive.
